title: Zinc Is in the d-Block, So Why Is It Not a Transition Metal?
subject: Chemistry
objective: A transition element has an incompletely filled d subshell in its atom or in a common ion. Iron (3d⁶) passes; copper (3d¹⁰ atom) passes through Cu²⁺ (3d⁹); zinc stays 3d¹⁰ even as Zn²⁺, so Zn, Cd and Hg are d-block but not transition metals.

fill.q: A transition element has an incompletely filled ____ subshell in its atom or a common ion.
When Zn forms Zn²⁺, the two ____ electrons leave.
Zn, Cd and Hg belong to group ____.

tf.q: Copper is a transition metal even though its atom is 3d¹⁰.

ar.r: Cu²⁺ has an incompletely filled 3d subshell.

ar.a: Mercury is not regarded as a transition metal.
ar.r: Mercury is a liquid at room temperature.
ar.explain: Both true; R does not explain A: the reason is its full 5d¹⁰ subshell.
